statement.p: Let \vec F= x\,\mathit{\vec i}+\left(x+y\right)\,\mathit{\vec j}+\left(x-y+z\right)\,\mathit{\vec k}. Let the line l be x = -\left(1+4t\right), y = 1+5t, z = -\left(4+3t\right).
(a) Find a point P = (x_0, y_0, z_0) where \vec F is parallel to l.
Find a point Q = (x_1,y_1,z_1) at which \vec F and l are perpendicular.
Give an equation for the set of all points at which \vec F and l are perpendicular.

static.solution:
(a) The line l is parallel to the vector \vec v = 4\,\mathit{\vec i}-2\,\mathit{\vec j}-2\,\mathit{\vec k}. The vector field \vec F is parallel to the line when \vec F is a multiple of \vec v. Taking the multiple to be 1 and solving for x,y,z, we find the point P = \left(-4,9,10\right). Other answers are possible.
(b) The line and vector field are perpendicular if \vec F\cdot\vec v=0, that is (x)(-4) + (x + y)(5) + (x - y + z)(-3) = 0. Solving, we can find any number of possibilities. One of these is Q = \left(3,0,-2\right).
(c) The set of all points that is perpendicular to the line is the equation shown in (b), -4x+5\mathopen{}\left(x+y\right)+\left(-3\right)\mathopen{}\left(x-y+z\right) = 0. This is a plane through the origin.
